answer.rationale: The p99 latency spike coincides temporally with a release 2 hours ago; this is the highest-confidence signal. Rollback is reversible, preserves write safety (memory_b2 warns against failover during heavy writes), and has demonstrated success clearing checkout errors without customer impact (memory_b1). Settlement traffic at peak and heavy writes rule out regional failover (replication gap risk) and read replica routing (doesn't address write path). Capacity addition would take longer to provision. Rollback offers fastest path to restore target latency while settlement traffic remains hot. The staged release approach (memory_b6) suggests the regression may not have been caught in canary; rolling back to the prior stable build (memory_b1 precedent) is the appropriate intervention when latency has degraded 5x in the post-release window.
